claims.statement: The training material is the WHO Global curriculum guide for community health workers, published in 2025.
claims.quote: Global curriculum guide for community health workers. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2025.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide adopts the principles and structure of competency-based education.
claims.quote: This CHW curriculum guide adopts the principles and structure of competency-based education (CBE).
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide describes CBE as oriented to outcome abilities with less emphasis on time-based training.
claims.quote: CBE aims to prepare learners for practice that is oriented to outcome abilities, with less emphasis on time-based training and increased attention to mastery of knowledge, skills and competencies for practice, as well as accountability, flexibility and lifelong learning (5).
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide is designed primarily for formal CHWs who are integrated into the health system and have a structured education pathway, a contract, remuneration and support.
claims.quote: This curriculum guide is designed primarily for formal CHWs who are integrated into the health system, who have a structured education pathway and a contract, and who are appropriately remunerated and supported.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.quote: There are three parts to this curriculum guide.
claims.locator: 3.1 Overview of the CHW curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The content comprises six competency domains, 12 universal modules (11 practice-activity modules and one basic science module), and four role-specific modules with 28 topics.
claims.quote: The content is organized into six competency domains, 12 universal modules (11 practice activities plus one module of basic science knowledge), and four role-specific modules, comprising 28 role-specific topics organized under the four modules.
claims.locator: 3.1 Overview of the CHW curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide contains 25 competencies, which it describes as relevant to all CHWs across all contexts.
claims.quote: There are 25 competencies that are relevant to all CHWs across all contexts, including the breadth of the practice activities in the universal and role-specific modules.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The universal modules are relevant to all CHWs, with contextualization.
claims.quote: These modules are relevant to all CHWs, with contextualization.
claims.locator: 3.1 Overview of the CHW curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The suggested total duration of the universal modules is 303 hours.
claims.quote: Total duration of universal practice activities (hours) 303
claims.locator: Table 2.1 Universal modules: practice activities and suggested duration
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: Role-specific areas include maternal and newborn health, HIV and STIs, tuberculosis, malaria, noncommunicable diseases, neglected tropical diseases, and health emergency preparedness and response.
claims.quote: These areas include maternal and newborn health, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and sexually transmitted infections (STIs), tuberculosis (TB), malaria, noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), and health emergency preparedness and response.
claims.locator: 3.1 Overview of the CHW curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: Role-specific content should be selected according to population needs and CHWs' scope of practice in a given context.
claims.quote: Content from the role-specific modules should therefore be selected based on the needs of the population and the scope of practice of CHWs in a given context.
claims.locator: 3.1 Overview of the CHW curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The home visit module suggests 33 teaching hours, including a minimum of 5 hours of shadowing and 6 hours of summative assessment.
claims.quote: The total suggested time to complete this module is 33 teaching hours, including a minimum of 5 hours of shadowing and 6 hours for the summative assessment (including 3 hours of practice-based observation).
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: Suggested learning activities include individual, small group and shadowing experiences.
claims.quote: These include a range of individual, small group and shadowing learning experiences to collectively build the knowledge, skills, attitudes and competencies for practice.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide states that teaching should minimize didactic approaches and use practical and authentic learning methods.
claims.quote: As recommended in the CHW guideline, teaching should minimize didactic approaches, and include a diverse array of practical and authentic learning methods suited to the unique needs and contexts of the learners.
claims.locator: Creating user-friendly learning materials appropriate to CHWs
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: Each module outlines both formative and summative assessments.
claims.quote: Both formative and summative assessments of learning are outlined for each module.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The summative assessment takes place at the end of the module to assess competence to perform the practice activity.
claims.quote: The summative assessment should take place at the end of the module, after the completion of learning activities, to assess competence to perform the practice activity or activities.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide proposes learning activities but does not contain the learning materials or case studies.
claims.quote: While it proposes learning activities that often draw from presentations, case scenarios or role play scenario cards, it does not contain the learning materials or case studies.
claims.locator: Creating user-friendly learning materials appropriate to CHWs

claims.statement: The guide describes itself as not intended to be rigid or prescriptive.
claims.quote: This guide is designed to facilitate design and implementation of CHW curricula, and is not intended to be interpreted as rigid or prescriptive.
claims.locator: 3.3 How to use the curriculum guide
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly

claims.statement: The guide states that maintaining CHWs' knowledge, skills and attitudes depends not only on summative assessment but also on continuous training, supportive supervision and follow-up engagement.
claims.quote: It is crucial to emphasize that ensuring that CHWs acquire and maintain the knowledge, skills and attitudes required for optimal performance of practice activities relies not solely on summative assessments on completion of training, but also on access to continuous training, supportive supervision, and follow-up engagement.
claims.reason: every citation quotes the source exactly
